495: ### Skill README Frontmatter Template
496: 
497: **Required Fields**: `title`, `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `version`
498: 
499: This is the `README.md` that sits beside a `SKILL.md`. [frontmatter-versioning.md](../references/frontmatter-versioning.md) lists `README.md` among the classes that must carry `version`, so the block is required there rather than optional.
500: 
501: ```yaml
502: ---
503: title: "skill-or-mode-name"
504: description: "One line saying what the skill does and who reaches for it."
505: trigger_phrases:
506:   - "distinctive phrase one"
507:   - "distinctive phrase two"
508:   - "distinctive phrase three"
509: version: 1.0.0.0
510: ---
511: ```
512: 
513: **Complete Example** (`sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/README.md`):
514: 
515: ```yaml
516: ---
517: title: "create-changelog"
518: description: "Writes a correctly versioned, correctly placed changelog entry from a spec folder, a component hint or git history, for anyone recording a shipped change."
519: trigger_phrases:
520:   - "create changelog"
521:   - "release notes"
522: version: 1.0.0.0
523: ---
524: ```
525: 
526: - `importance_tier` and `contextType` are optional here. A minority of skill READMEs carry them. No validator asks for them.
527: - READMEs deeper in a skill tree are a different class. Most carry no block at all. `sk-create-readme`'s own template treats frontmatter as optional for a normal project README, so add a block to one of those only when the document should be discoverable.
528: - Nothing enforces the field set. The advisor's `check-skill-doc-frontmatter.sh`, under `system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/`, exempts `README.md`, so the version gate is the only automated check a README block faces.
529: - `trigger_phrases` lengths across skill READMEs run from 2 items to 13. The 3 to 8 range in Section 3 is the reference and asset rule, not a README rule.
530: 
531: ### Feature Catalog Frontmatter Template
532: 
533: **Required Fields**: `title`, `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `version`
534: 
535: A catalog has two document shapes and they differ by one field. Per-feature leaf card:
536: 
537: ```yaml
538: ---
539: title: "Feature name"
540: description: "One line, shown in the root catalog table."
541: trigger_phrases:
542:   - "the H3 feature heading from the root catalog"
543:   - "a natural-language alternate"
544:   - "the tool or command name"
545: version: 1.0.0.0
546: ---
547: ```
548: 
549: Root index, which adds `last_updated`:
550: 
551: ```yaml
552: ---
553: title: "<skill>: Feature Catalog"
554: description: "Current-state inventory for <skill>, covering <surfaces>."
555: trigger_phrases:
556:   - "<skill> feature catalog"
557:   - "<skill> capabilities"
558: last_updated: "2026-08-23"
559: version: 1.0.0.0
560: ---
561: ```
562: 
563: - The four leaf fields are the settled shape. 809 of the 878 leaf cards in the tree use exactly those and no others.
564: - `last_updated` is a root habit rather than a leaf one. It appears on 19 of 27 roots against 6 of 878 leaves, always as a quoted ISO date.
565: - `importance_tier` is optional and `contextType` is not part of this class. Each appears on well under a tenth of leaves.
566: - Catalog `trigger_phrases` route nothing today, because the advisor doc-trigger harvest scans `references/` and `assets/` only. The field is still required. It is what a reader searches on, so match it to the root catalog H3 heading.
567: - The field-by-field contract lives in `sk-create-feature-catalog/assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` Section 2.
568: 
569: ### Testing Playbook Frontmatter Template
570: 
571: **Required Fields**: `title`, `description`, `version`
572: 
573: Those three are the whole settled block, for the root index and for a per-feature scenario alike. `trigger_phrases` is not part of this class.
574: 
575: ```yaml
576: ---
577: title: "OBS-009 -- Register and inspect the official CLI"
578: description: "This scenario validates official obsidian CLI registration and help output in an app-backed environment."
579: version: 1.0.0.0
580: ---
581: ```
582: 
583: Root index, same three fields with a `<skill>: Manual Testing Playbook` title:
584: 
585: ```yaml
586: ---
587: title: "create-frontmatter: Manual Testing Playbook"
588: description: "Operator-facing reference combining the testing directory, execution expectations and the per-feature validation files for this packet."
589: version: 1.0.0.0
590: ---
591: ```
592: 
593: **Past those three fields this class has no settled convention.** Playbook leaves in this repository carry a long tail of runner-specific keys, among them `id`, `stage`, `category`, `expected_intent`, `expected_resources`, `expected_workflow_mode`, `expected_leaf_resources`, `matrix_cell`, `test_file`, `test_name` and `playbook_path`. No set of them is standard: the largest shape past the core covers 193 of 1,728 leaves. Each key belongs to whichever runner reads it. Add one only when a runner reads it. Never copy a set across from a neighbouring playbook.
594: 
595: Two of those keys change behavior rather than describing it:
596: 
597: | Key | What it does |
598: |-----|--------------|
599: | `id`, `expected_intent`, `expected_resources` | Any one of them enrols the scenario in the routing-gold topology gate, and the compiled-routing scenario validator rejects a compiled-routing scenario that lacks one. |
600: | `stage` | Benchmark tier, one of `routing`, `holdout` or `negative`. It carries what a numbered filename prefix used to encode. |
601: 
602: Both are documented in `sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/assets/manual-testing-playbook-snippet-template.md` Section 2.
603: 
604: ### Agent Frontmatter Template
605: 
606: **Required Fields**: `name`, `description`, plus the authority key its own runtime reads.
607: 
608: An agent has no single block. The field set is chosen by the directory the file lives in. The other runtime authority key is silently ignored rather than rejected, which is why the wrong one is a security defect and not a validation error.
609: 
610: `.skilled/agents/` uses a `permission:` object:
611: 
612: ```yaml
613: ---
614: name: agent-name
615: description: One line covering purpose, authority and the main boundary.
616: mode: subagent
617: temperature: 0.1
618: permission:
619:   read: allow
620:   write: allow
621:   edit: allow
622:   bash: allow
623:   grep: allow
624:   glob: allow
625:   list: allow
626:   memory: allow
627:   webfetch: deny
628:   chrome_devtools: deny
629:   task: deny
630:   patch: deny
631: mcpServers:
632:   - system_skill_advisor
633: ---
634: ```
635: 
636: `.claude/agents/` and `.cursor/agents/` use a `tools:` allow-list:
637: 
638: ```yaml

640: name: agent-name
641: description: One line covering purpose, authority and the main boundary.
642: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
643: ---

690: trigger_phrases:

721:   - "<component> <version>"

723: importance_tier: "normal"
724: contextType: "general"

983: ## 7. AUTO-GENERATION GUIDELINES
984: 
985: ### Field Inference Rules
986: 
987: When auto-generating frontmatter, infer values from document content:
988: 
989: **`name` Field**:
990: ```
991: Source: Parent directory name
992: Method: Extract from file path
993: 
994: Example:
995:   Input: .skilled/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
996:   Output: my-skill
997: ```
998: 
999: **`description` Field**:
1000: ```
1001: Source: H1 subtitle or first paragraph
1002: Method: 
1003:   1. Look for " - " in H1 (e.g., "# Skill Name - Description")
1004:   2. Fallback to first paragraph after H1
1005: 
1006: Example:
1007:   H1: "# My Skill - Brief description of purpose"
1008:   Output: "Brief description of purpose"
1009: ```
1010: 
1011: **`argument-hint` Field** (Commands):
1012: ```
1013: Source: INPUTS section or CONTRACT section
1014: Method: Extract from Required/Optional input lists
1015: 
1016: Example:
1017:   Content:
1018:     ### Required Inputs
1019:     - `name`: Skill name
1020:     ### Optional Inputs  
1021:     - `version`: Version number
1022:   
1023:   Output: <name> [version]
1024: ```
1025: 
1026: **`allowed-tools` Field**:
1027: ```
1028: Source: WORKFLOW section code examples
1029: Method: Extract tool names from code blocks
1030: 
1031: Example:
1032:   Content:
1033:     ```
1034:     Read("file.md")
1035:     Write("output.md", content)
1036:     Bash("ls -la")
1037:     ```
1038:   
1039:   Output: Read, Write, Bash
1040: ```
1041: 
1042: ### Auto-Generation Decision Tree
1043: 
1044: ```
1045: Document type detected?
1046: ├─► SKILL.md
1047: │   ├─ Has frontmatter? → Validate fields
1048: │   └─ Missing frontmatter? → Auto-generate + ask user to review
1049: │
1050: ├─► Command
1051: │   ├─ Has frontmatter? → Validate fields
1052: │   └─ Missing frontmatter? → Auto-generate from content
1053: │
1054: ├─► Skill Reference/Asset
1055: │   ├─ Has 5-field block? → Validate fields (trigger_phrases 3-8, enums)
1056: │   └─ Missing fields? → Author from doc content (title from H1, phrases from headings)
1057: │
1058: ├─► Knowledge (outside skills)
1059: │   ├─ Has frontmatter? → Remove it
1060: │   └─ No frontmatter? → Valid (no action)
1061: │
1062: ├─► Spec folder document
1063: │   ├─ Has frontmatter? → Validate required fields (title, description, trigger_phrases, importance_tier, _memory.continuity)
1064: │   └─ No frontmatter? → Auto-generate from Spec Kit template
1065: │
1066: └─► README
1067:     ├─ Beside a SKILL.md? → Validate title, description,
1068:     │                      trigger_phrases, version
1069:     └─ Elsewhere? → Optional, no action when absent
1070: ```
1071: 
1072: ---
1073: 
1074: ## 8. INTERACTIVE WORKFLOW
1075: 
1076: ### Adding Frontmatter Interactively
1077: 
1078: **Step 1: Present Inferred Template**
1079: ```

1083: Type: SKILL.md (frontmatter required)

1085: Proposed frontmatter (inferred from document):
1086: ---
1087: name: new-skill
1088: description: Brief description inferred from H1 subtitle
1089: allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash
1090: ---
1091: 
1092: Options:
1093: 1. Accept as-is
1094: 2. Edit values before applying
1095: 3. Skip (leave non-compliant)
1096: 
1097: Choice:
1098: ```
1099: 
1100: **Step 2: Edit Values (if selected)**
1101: ```
1102: Edit frontmatter values:
1103: 
1104: name [new-skill]: _
1105: description [Brief description...]: _
1106: allowed-tools [Read, Write, Bash]: _
1107: 
1108: Press Enter to keep default, or type new value.

1110: 
1111: **Step 3: Apply**
1112: ```bash

1114: {
1115:   echo "---"
1116:   echo "name: $name"
1117:   echo "description: $description"
1118:   echo "allowed-tools: $allowed_tools"
1119:   echo "---"
1120:   echo ""
1121:   cat original_file.md
1122: } > updated_file.md
1123: ```

1126: 
1127: ## 9. BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY
1128: 
1129: ### DO
1130: 
1131: | Practice | Reason |
1132: |----------|--------|
1133: | Keep description on single line | Parser limitation |
1134: | Match `name` to directory name | Consistency, discoverability |
1135: | Order tools by frequency | Most used first |
1136: | Use exact tool names | Case-sensitive matching |
1137: | Validate before committing | Catch errors early |
1138: 
1139: ### DON'T
1140: 
1141: | Anti-Pattern | Problem |
1142: |--------------|---------|
1143: | Multiline descriptions | Won't parse correctly |
1144: | Uppercase in `name` | Violates format requirement |
1145: | Frontmatter on knowledge files outside skills | Implies programmatic interface |
1146: | Bare title+description on skill references/assets | Advisor doc harvest needs the full 5-field block |
1147: | Empty required fields | Validation failure |
1148: | Made-up tool names | Tools won't be available |
1149: 
1150: ---
1151: 
1152: ## 10. QUICK REFERENCE
1153: 
1154: ### Frontmatter Decision Tree
1155: 
1156: ```
1157: Document type?
1158: ├─► SKILL.md             → MUST have: name, description, allowed-tools
1159: ├─► Command              → MUST have: description, argument-hint, allowed-tools
1160: ├─► Skill Reference/Asset → MUST have: title, description, trigger_phrases,
1161: │                           importance_tier, contextType (README.md exempt)
1162: ├─► Knowledge (outside skills) → MUST NOT have frontmatter (remove if present)
1163: ├─► Spec folder doc      → MUST have frontmatter (system-spec-kit owns the block)
1164: └─► README               → Beside a SKILL.md: title, description,
1165:                             trigger_phrases, version. Elsewhere optional
1166: ```
1167: 
1168: ### Field Requirements Matrix
1169: 
1170: | Document Type | name | description | argument-hint | allowed-tools |
1171: |---------------|------|-------------|---------------|---------------|
1172: | **SKILL.md** | ✅ Required | ✅ Required | ❌ N/A | ✅ Required |
1173: | **Command** | ⚪ Optional | ✅ Required | ✅ Required | ✅ Required |
1174: | **Skill Reference/Asset** | ❌ Not used (uses `title`) | ✅ Required | ❌ N/A | ❌ N/A |
1175: | **Knowledge (outside skills)** | ❌ Forbidden | ❌ Forbidden | ❌ Forbidden | ❌ Forbidden |
1176: | **Spec** | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a (see `system-spec-kit`) |
1177: | **Changelog entry** | ❌ Not used (uses `title`) | ✅ Required | ❌ N/A | ❌ N/A |
1178: | **Feature Catalog** | ❌ Not used (uses `title`) | ✅ Required | ❌ N/A | ❌ N/A |
1179: | **Testing Playbook** | ❌ Not used (uses `title`) | ✅ Required | ❌ N/A | ❌ N/A |
1180: | **Agent** | ✅ Required | ✅ Required | ❌ N/A | ❌ N/A (uses `permission:` or `tools:`) |
1181: 
1182: - Skill references/assets also require `trigger_phrases` (3-8), `importance_tier`, `contextType` and `version`. See Section 3.
1183: - Changelog entries also require `trigger_phrases`, `importance_tier` and `contextType`.
1184: - Feature catalogs additionally require `trigger_phrases` and `version`.
1185: - Testing playbooks require `title` and `version`.
1186: - Agents require the authority key their own runtime reads, and carry no `version`.
1187: 
1188: Section 4 has a template for each class.
1189: 
1190: ### Common Mistakes
1191: 
1192: | Mistake | Fix |
1193: |---------|-----|
1194: | Non-skill knowledge file with frontmatter | Remove frontmatter |
1195: | Skill reference/asset missing the 5-field block | Author trigger_phrases (3-8), importance_tier, contextType |
1196: | SKILL.md missing `name` | Add with directory name |
1197: | Command missing `argument-hint` | Infer from content or ask |
1198: | Spec folder doc missing its block | Restore it from the `system-spec-kit` template |
1199: | Wrong field names (Name vs name) | Use lowercase field names |
1200: | Multiline description | Collapse to single line |

490: Verify with `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/check-skill-doc-frontmatter.sh`. Two things about that checker decide what a green run means:
491: 
492: - Its default `--shape` mode fails only a document that carries a partial block, so a file with `title` and `description` alone, or with no block at all, passes. Pass `--coverage` to require the full block.
493: - It walks `references/` and `assets/` directly under each top-level skill folder only, so the docs of a nested mode packet are never read by it. For those, `package_skill.py --check --strict` on the packet is the gate that reaches the block.
494: 
495: ### Skill README Frontmatter Template
496: 
497: **Required Fields**: `title`, `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `version`
498: 
499: This is the `README.md` that sits beside a `SKILL.md`. [frontmatter-versioning.md](../references/frontmatter-versioning.md) lists `README.md` among the classes that must carry `version`, so the block is required there rather than optional.
500: 
501: ```yaml
502: ---
503: title: "skill-or-mode-name"
504: description: "One line saying what the skill does and who reaches for it."
505: trigger_phrases:
506:   - "distinctive phrase one"
507:   - "distinctive phrase two"
508:   - "distinctive phrase three"
509: version: 1.0.0.0
510: ---
511: ```
512: 
513: **Complete Example** (`sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/README.md`):
514: 
515: ```yaml
516: ---
517: title: "create-changelog"
518: description: "Writes a correctly versioned, correctly placed changelog entry from a spec folder, a component hint or git history, for anyone recording a shipped change."
519: trigger_phrases:
520:   - "create changelog"
521:   - "release notes"
522: version: 1.0.0.0
523: ---
524: ```
525: 
526: - `importance_tier` and `contextType` are optional here. A minority of skill READMEs carry them. No validator asks for them.
527: - READMEs deeper in a skill tree are a different class. Most carry no block at all. `sk-create-readme`'s own template treats frontmatter as optional for a normal project README, so add a block to one of those only when the document should be discoverable.
528: - Nothing enforces the field set. The advisor's `check-skill-doc-frontmatter.sh`, under `system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/`, exempts `README.md`, so the version gate is the only automated check a README block faces.
529: - `trigger_phrases` lengths across skill READMEs run from 2 items to 13. The 3 to 8 range in Section 3 is the reference and asset rule, not a README rule.
530: 
531: ### Feature Catalog Frontmatter Template
532: 
533: **Required Fields**: `title`, `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `version`
534: 
535: A catalog has two document shapes and they differ by one field. Per-feature leaf card:
536: 
537: ```yaml
538: ---
539: title: "Feature name"
540: description: "One line, shown in the root catalog table."
541: trigger_phrases:
542:   - "the H3 feature heading from the root catalog"
543:   - "a natural-language alternate"
544:   - "the tool or command name"
545: version: 1.0.0.0
546: ---
547: ```
548: 
549: Root index, which adds `last_updated`:
550: 
551: ```yaml
552: ---
553: title: "<skill>: Feature Catalog"
554: description: "Current-state inventory for <skill>, covering <surfaces>."
555: trigger_phrases:
556:   - "<skill> feature catalog"
557:   - "<skill> capabilities"
558: last_updated: "2026-08-23"
559: version: 1.0.0.0
560: ---
561: ```
562: 
563: - The four leaf fields are the settled shape. 809 of the 878 leaf cards in the tree use exactly those and no others.
564: - `last_updated` is a root habit rather than a leaf one. It appears on 19 of 27 roots against 6 of 878 leaves, always as a quoted ISO date.
565: - `importance_tier` is optional and `contextType` is not part of this class. Each appears on well under a tenth of leaves.
566: - Catalog `trigger_phrases` route nothing today, because the advisor doc-trigger harvest scans `references/` and `assets/` only. The field is still required. It is what a reader searches on, so match it to the root catalog H3 heading.
567: - The field-by-field contract lives in `sk-create-feature-catalog/assets/feature-catalog-snippet-template.md` Section 2.
568: 
569: ### Testing Playbook Frontmatter Template
570: 
571: **Required Fields**: `title`, `description`, `version`
572: 
573: Those three are the whole settled block, for the root index and for a per-feature scenario alike. `trigger_phrases` is not part of this class.
574: 
575: ```yaml
576: ---
577: title: "OBS-009 -- Register and inspect the official CLI"
578: description: "This scenario validates official obsidian CLI registration and help output in an app-backed environment."
579: version: 1.0.0.0
580: ---
581: ```
582: 
583: Root index, same three fields with a `<skill>: Manual Testing Playbook` title:
584: 
585: ```yaml
586: ---
587: title: "create-frontmatter: Manual Testing Playbook"
588: description: "Operator-facing reference combining the testing directory, execution expectations and the per-feature validation files for this packet."
589: version: 1.0.0.0
590: ---
591: ```
592: 
593: **Past those three fields this class has no settled convention.** Playbook leaves in this repository carry a long tail of runner-specific keys, among them `id`, `stage`, `category`, `expected_intent`, `expected_resources`, `expected_workflow_mode`, `expected_leaf_resources`, `matrix_cell`, `test_file`, `test_name` and `playbook_path`. No set of them is standard: the largest shape past the core covers 193 of 1,728 leaves. Each key belongs to whichever runner reads it. Add one only when a runner reads it. Never copy a set across from a neighbouring playbook.
594: 
595: Two of those keys change behavior rather than describing it:
596: 
597: | Key | What it does |
598: |-----|--------------|
599: | `id`, `expected_intent`, `expected_resources` | Any one of them enrols the scenario in the routing-gold topology gate, and the compiled-routing scenario validator rejects a compiled-routing scenario that lacks one. |
600: | `stage` | Benchmark tier, one of `routing`, `holdout` or `negative`. It carries what a numbered filename prefix used to encode. |
601: 
602: Both are documented in `sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/assets/manual-testing-playbook-snippet-template.md` Section 2.
603: 
604: ### Agent Frontmatter Template
605: 
606: **Required Fields**: `name`, `description`, plus the authority key its own runtime reads.
607: 
608: An agent has no single block. The field set is chosen by the directory the file lives in. The other runtime authority key is silently ignored rather than rejected, which is why the wrong one is a security defect and not a validation error.
609: 
610: `.skilled/agents/` uses a `permission:` object:
611: 
612: ```yaml
613: ---
614: name: agent-name
615: description: One line covering purpose, authority and the main boundary.
616: mode: subagent
617: temperature: 0.1
618: permission:
619:   read: allow
620:   write: allow
621:   edit: allow
622:   bash: allow
623:   grep: allow
624:   glob: allow
625:   list: allow
626:   memory: allow
627:   webfetch: deny
628:   chrome_devtools: deny
629:   task: deny
630:   patch: deny
631: mcpServers:
632:   - system_skill_advisor
633: ---
634: ```
635: 
636: `.claude/agents/` and `.cursor/agents/` use a `tools:` allow-list:
637: 
638: ```yaml
639: ---
640: name: agent-name
641: description: One line covering purpose, authority and the main boundary.
642: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
643: ---
644: ```
645: 
646: `.pi/agents/` carries the same three keys with `tools` as a block list of lowercase names.
647: 
648: - **No `version`.** The versioning standard puts `.skilled/agents/*.md` out of scope. No agent file in the tree carries one.
649: - `validate_document.py` blocks a `.claude/agents/` file that has no non-empty `tools:`, because Claude Code enforces only `tools:` and an absent list inherits the parent session full, unrestricted tool set. It blocks a `.skilled/agents/` file with no `permission:` and warns on a stray `tools:` there.
650: - `mode` is `subagent` on all but two OpenCode agents in the tree. `temperature` sits at 0.1 or 0.2. `mcpServers` is optional and rare.
651: - Keep `description` at 130 characters or fewer. Agent descriptions share the Claude Code metadata budget described above.
652: - `template-rules.json` lists `name`, `description`, `mode`, `temperature` and `permission` as required for the agent type without splitting by runtime. That list is not read for agents, since `validate_document.py` consults `frontmatterFields.required` only on the command and changelog paths. The runtime split is what runs.
653: - The fuller field reference is `sk-create-agent/assets/agent-template.md` Section 2.
654: 
655: ### Knowledge File Outside Skill Folders (No Frontmatter)
656: 
657: **Rule**: Knowledge files outside `.skilled/skills/*/` should **NOT** have YAML frontmatter. (Skill references/assets are covered by the 5-field block above instead.)
658: 
659: ```markdown
660: # ❌ BEFORE (incorrect)
661: ---
662: name: document-style-guide
663: description: Style guide for documentation
664: ---
665: 
666: # Document Style Guide
667: 
668: Content...
669: 
670: # ✅ AFTER (correct)
671: # Document Style Guide
672: 
673: Content...
674: ```
675: 
676: ### Spec File (Governed by `system-spec-kit`)
677: 
678: **Rule**: Spec-folder documents carry YAML frontmatter, and this contract does not define it.
679: 
680: `system-spec-kit` owns the block. Its `templates/core/spec.md.tmpl` emits one at every level, and
681: `validate.sh --strict` prints `RESULT: FAILED` on a `spec.md` whose block is missing or malformed. A
682: missing block trips the frontmatter-basics check, which reports the absent `_memory.continuity` keys,
683: and a malformed one trips `SPECDOC_FRONTMATTER_001`. The keys are that skill's, including the `_memory.continuity` mapping no other
684: class carries, so read them there rather than composing a block from this section.
685: 
686: ```yaml
687: ---
688: title: "Feature Specification: <name>"
689: description: "One line on what the packet does."
690: trigger_phrases:
691:   - "distinctive phrase"
692: importance_tier: "important"
693: contextType: "implementation"
694: _memory:
695:   continuity:
696:     packet_pointer: "<track>/<packet>"
697: ---
698: ```
699: 
700: **Where to go**: the templates under `system-spec-kit/templates/`, and the scaffold that fills them.
701: Never hand-author a spec block from this page, and never strip one you find.
702: 
703: ### Changelog Entry (Governed by `sk-create-changelog`)
704: 
705: **Rule**: A changelog entry carries YAML frontmatter, and `sk-create-changelog` defines it.
706: 
707: An entry is a `v{VERSION}.md` file in a skill's or the release line's `changelog/` folder, or a
708: `changelog-*.md` file in a spec packet's `changelog/` folder. Its block carries `title`,
709: `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `importance_tier` and `contextType` in that order, so Gate 1 and
710: `/speckit:search` find the entry the way they find a spec document. The identity phrases come first.
711: `validate_document.py` blocks an entry that has no block, lacks a key or declares no trigger phrase.
712: It also blocks a version entry whose phrases never name its version. A README in a changelog folder is not an
713: entry and keeps the structural rules alone.
714: 
715: ```yaml
716: ---
717: title: "<component> v<version>, <editorial title>"
718: description: "One or two plain sentences on what the release changed."
719: trigger_phrases:
720:   - "<component> v<version>"
721:   - "<component> <version>"
722:   - "<topic phrase from the entry>"
723: importance_tier: "normal"
724: contextType: "general"
725: ---
726: ```
727: 
728: **Where to go**: the Frontmatter Contract in section 5 of `sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md` for skill and
729: release entries. Packet-local changelogs are deprecated, and existing ones keep the block the nested generator renders.
730: 
731: ---

Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.

**Core Purpose**:
- **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
- **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
- **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
- **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
- **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting

**Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
- AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
- Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic

```
Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
         └─ Always in context (~100 words)
            ↓
Level 2: SKILL.md body
         └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
            ↓

**Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

The machine router for [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md). `SKILL.md` keeps the short routing prose and the
link that points here; this file holds the declaration a reader parses to decide what loads.

## 1. OVERVIEW

The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
loads before an intent selects it.

---

## 2. INTENT MODEL

[TODO: Write one bullet per `INTENT_SIGNALS` key: the intent, the phrasing that fires it, and the exact files it loads.]

[TODO: Keep this section and the machine block below in sync. When a row changes here, change the matching map entry.]

A skill may name its intent map `INTENT_MODEL` instead of `INTENT_SIGNALS`, the name this template and the replay
reader both accept. Declaring both is legal only when they mirror each other exactly, in keys and in keywords;
otherwise keep one. A router may also route by pseudocode alone with no map at all, which suits a skill that loads
its whole reference set on any match, because a hub's map is the one thing this flexibility never relaxes.

---

## 3. MACHINE ROUTER

The one machine-readable projection of the intent model above, written as `## MACHINE ROUTER` so every
reader finds it. This section is the last in the file, and it holds the only pseudocode.

```python
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")

# The document every run loads before intent scoring. [TODO: replace this scaffold default.]
DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "{{DEFAULT_RESOURCE}}"

INTENT_SIGNALS = {
    "PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["{{SKILL_NAME}}", "{{SKILL_NAME}} workflow"]},
}

RESOURCE_MAP = {
    "PRIMARY": ["{{DEFAULT_RESOURCE}}"],
}

# Every key above must appear in both maps, and every path must resolve inside this folder.
# An intent that deliberately loads nothing may be listed in NO_LOAD_INTENTS, which is the only way a key may sit
# outside RESOURCE_MAP or map to an empty list; that list is checked, so an intent that loses its resources by
# accident still fails. A markdown file at this router's own root, which no leaf manifest lists, may be routed by
# declaring it in ROOT_RESOURCES and referencing it from a RESOURCE_MAP entry.
# None of these three patterns is available to a hub router.
UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
    "Confirm the task intent",
    "Provide one concrete input or expected output",
    "Confirm the verification command set before completion",
]

def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
    docs = []
    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
        if base.exists():
            docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}

def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
    if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
        raise ValueError(f"Only skill-local markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()

def route_resources(request):
    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
    selected = select_resources_for_request(request, inventory)
    if not selected:
        return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "needs_disambiguation": True, "resources": [], "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}

    loaded = []
    for relative_path in selected:
        guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in loaded:
            load(guarded)
            loaded.append(guarded)
    return {"resources": loaded}
```

A request that matches no intent returns `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with that checklist, never a silent default
and never an empty result. Replace `select_resources_for_request` with the domain-specific selection
logic, and keep the guarded load: the guard is what keeps a path inside this skill folder.

# {{SKILL_TITLE}} Router

The machine router for [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md). `SKILL.md` keeps the short routing prose and the
link that points here; this file holds the declaration a reader parses to decide what loads.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

[TODO: Name the families of request signals that reach this skill, and the families of resources the router selects from. Leave the exact keywords, the exact paths and the default resource to INTENT MODEL.]

The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
loads before an intent selects it.

---

## 2. INTENT MODEL

[TODO: Write one bullet per `INTENT_SIGNALS` key: the intent, the phrasing that fires it, and the exact files it loads.]

[TODO: Keep this section and the machine block below in sync. When a row changes here, change the matching map entry.]

A skill may name its intent map `INTENT_MODEL` instead of `INTENT_SIGNALS`, the name this template and the replay
reader both accept. Declaring both is legal only when they mirror each other exactly, in keys and in keywords;
otherwise keep one. A router may also route by pseudocode alone with no map at all, which suits a skill that loads
its whole reference set on any match, because a hub's map is the one thing this flexibility never relaxes.

---

## 3. MACHINE ROUTER

The one machine-readable projection of the intent model above, written as `## MACHINE ROUTER` so every
reader finds it. This section is the last in the file, and it holds the only pseudocode.

```python
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")

# The document every run loads before intent scoring. [TODO: replace this scaffold default.]
DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "{{DEFAULT_RESOURCE}}"

INTENT_SIGNALS = {
    "PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["{{SKILL_NAME}}", "{{SKILL_NAME}} workflow"]},
}

RESOURCE_MAP = {
    "PRIMARY": ["{{DEFAULT_RESOURCE}}"],
}

# Every key above must appear in both maps, and every path must resolve inside this folder.
# An intent that deliberately loads nothing may be listed in NO_LOAD_INTENTS, which is the only way a key may sit
# outside RESOURCE_MAP or map to an empty list; that list is checked, so an intent that loses its resources by
# accident still fails. A markdown file at this router's own root, which no leaf manifest lists, may be routed by
# declaring it in ROOT_RESOURCES and referencing it from a RESOURCE_MAP entry.
# None of these three patterns is available to a hub router.
UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
    "Confirm the task intent",
    "Provide one concrete input or expected output",
    "Confirm the verification command set before completion",
]

def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
    docs = []
    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
        if base.exists():
            docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
    return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}

def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
    if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
        raise ValueError(f"Only skill-local markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()

def route_resources(request):
    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
    selected = select_resources_for_request(request, inventory)
    if not selected:
        return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "needs_disambiguation": True, "resources": [], "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}

    loaded = []
    for relative_path in selected:
        guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in loaded:
            load(guarded)
            loaded.append(guarded)
    return {"resources": loaded}
```

A request that matches no intent returns `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with that checklist, never a silent default
and never an empty result. Replace `select_resources_for_request` with the domain-specific selection
logic, and keep the guarded load: the guard is what keeps a path inside this skill folder.

# README Template and Selection Guide

Use this template for project, skill, feature and component READMEs. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) for source-folder READMEs that explain package topology, files, boundaries and data or control flow.

---

## 1. README SELECTION

README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?

| Type | Use When | Template |
|---|---|---|
| Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
| Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
| Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
| Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
| Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |

Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.

```text
Is this a project, package, skill or feature root?
+-- Yes: write a general README.
`-- No: is this source-code orientation?
    +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
    `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
```

Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.

---

## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE

Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.

| Section | Include When | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
| Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
| How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
| Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
| Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
| Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
| Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
| Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
| Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
| Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
| FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
| Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |

Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).

---

## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE

Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.

| Profile Block | Good For | Keep It Short By |
|---|---|---|
| `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
| Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
| How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
| Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
| Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |
| Related Skills | Skill graph navigation | Group by relationship type |
| Related Documents | Operator or developer references | Link stable docs, not packet history |
| FAQ | Repeated questions | 3-6 high-value Q&A pairs |

Sections use plain numbered H2 headings. Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments or a Table of Contents.

```markdown
## 1. OVERVIEW

[Section content]

```

---

## 4. WRITING RULES

Write for scanning first.

- Lead with what the thing does.
- Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
- Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
- Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
- Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
- Test commands before documenting them.
- Show expected output for verification commands.
- Use relative links for local docs.
- Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.

The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:

```markdown
**`spec.md`**
- What the feature is and why it exists.
- Required at every level.
```

Group related items under an unnumbered `#####` heading when the inventory has natural groups, for example by how each item is triggered.

"""Check, or with --restore put back, the fenced code blocks of changed Markdown files under a directory to their HEAD text.

A block the orchestrator approved after reading it, such as a structure tree gaining a missing file,
is listed verbatim in approved-blocks.md beside the @scope file and counts as unchanged.
"""
import subprocess, sys, re, os
def targets(arg):
    """A directory, or @<file> listing paths one per line."""
    if arg.startswith('@'):
        return [l.strip() for l in open(arg[1:]) if l.strip()]
    return [arg]
d = sys.argv[1]; restore = '--restore' in sys.argv
fence = re.compile(r'^(```+|~~~+)[^\n]*\n.*?^\1[ \t]*$', re.S | re.M)
changed = mism = 0
allowed = set()
if d.startswith('@'):
    ap = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(d[1:]), 'approved-blocks.md')
    if os.path.exists(ap): allowed = {m.group(0) for m in fence.finditer(open(ap).read())}
for f in subprocess.run(['git', 'diff', '--name-only', 'HEAD', '--', *targets(d)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split():
    if not f.endswith('.md'): continue
    old = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{f}'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if old.returncode: continue
    ob = [m.group(0) for m in fence.finditer(old.stdout)]; cur = open(f).read(); cb = list(fence.finditer(cur))
    pool = list(ob); edited = []
    for m in cb:
        if m.group(0) in pool: pool.remove(m.group(0))
        else: edited.append(m)
    if allowed and len(edited) == len(pool):
        keep = [(m, o) for m, o in zip(edited, pool) if m.group(0) not in allowed]
        edited = [m for m, _ in keep]; pool = [o for _, o in keep]

"""List changed Markdown files under a directory whose frontmatter differs from HEAD, ignoring the version line."""
import subprocess, sys, re
def targets(arg):
    """A directory, or @<file> listing paths one per line."""
    if arg.startswith('@'):
        return [l.strip() for l in open(arg[1:]) if l.strip()]
    return [arg]
d = sys.argv[1]
files = subprocess.run(['git', 'diff', '--name-only', 'HEAD', '--', *targets(d)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
def fm(text):
    m = re.match(r'---\n(.*?)\n---\n', text, re.S)
    return [l for l in (m.group(1).split('\n') if m else []) if not l.startswith('version:')]
bad = 0
for f in files:
    if not f.endswith('.md'): continue
    old = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{f}'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if old.returncode: continue
    if fm(old.stdout) != fm(open(f).read()):
        bad += 1; print(f'FRONTMATTER-CHANGED {f}')
print(f'frontmatter_changed={bad}')

## 2. SCENARIO CONTRACT

Operators run the exact prompt and command sequence for `FMV-002` and confirm the expected signals without contradictory evidence.

- Objective: produce a gated real edit count for one file, show the ungated count beside it, and name the gap
- Realistic user request: `How many real edits has this file had? I need it for the version.`
- Prompt: `How many times has this file actually been edited? I need the build number for its version.`
- Expected execution process: `references/frontmatter-versioning.md` loads, section 4 supplies the real-edit-count rule, `git log --follow --numstat` is run for the single file, commits whose added-plus-deleted count for that file is zero are discarded, the surviving count becomes the build segment, and the ungated commit count is reported alongside it.
- Expected signals: two numbers are reported, the gated one is the smaller, the gap is named, and the two documented inflators are given as the reason. The build segment is capped, and brand-new files with zero or one commit report zero.
- Desired user-visible outcome: a gated count, the ungated count beside it, and the gap named.
- Pass/fail: PASS if both counts are shown and the gated one is used. FAIL if only one number is produced, if the gate is described but not run, or if the ungated count is used as the build segment.

### Commands

1. `agent: Read references/frontmatter-versioning.md section 4 and state the real edit count rule`
2. `bash: git log --follow --numstat -- .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md`

### Expected

Step 1 quotes the rule: the build segment counts commits whose own added-plus-deleted line count for that file is above zero, traced with `--follow` for continuity across renames and gated per file. Step 2 produces the raw material, one numstat block per commit, which is what makes the gate checkable rather than assertable. Step 3 yields two counts that differ. Step 4 names the gap and attributes it to the historical repository-wide move and to bulk sweep commits, and applies the cap on the build segment. A file with zero or one commit reports a build of zero.

### Evidence

Capture the prompt exactly as typed, the rule as quoted from section 4, the literal `git log --follow --numstat` transcript, the gated count, the ungated count, the gap between them, and the two inflators named. Both counts are required. The assertion in this scenario is a comparison, and a single number cannot be graded because a wrong build segment is a well-formed integer.

## 2. SCENARIO CONTRACT

Operators run the exact prompt and command sequence for `FMB-003` and confirm the expected signals without contradictory evidence.

- Objective: diagnose a silent discovery drop as a breach of the shared project-wide allowance, not as a per-file length problem
- Realistic user request: `A skill is no longer being suggested automatically, but it still runs when I ask for it by name.`
- Prompt: `One of our skills stopped showing up for the model, but it still works when I name it directly. Nothing errored. What happened?`
- Expected execution process: `assets/frontmatter-templates.md` loads, the budget section is read for the project total rather than the per-skill target, the answer identifies the drop as silent and as applying to the longest entries, and the remedy is described as trimming across the project rather than editing the affected file.
- Expected signals: the reply names the project total as a shared allowance, states that the longest entries are dropped and that skills stay explicitly invocable, and confirms that nothing warns at the point of failure. It does not conclude that the affected file's own description is too long without measuring it.
- Desired user-visible outcome: the user learns the cost is shared, that their own file may be fine, and which check surfaces accumulated drift.
- Pass/fail: PASS if the diagnosis names the shared project allowance and the silent drop of the longest entries. FAIL if the answer treats it as a per-file length rule, or asserts a cause with no reference to the budget table.

### Expected

Step 1 separates the two numbers. They have different scopes and only one of them explains this symptom. Step 2 matches the report to the documented behavior: over the project total, the longest descriptions are dropped from the available-skills list, the skills remain invocable explicitly, and nothing reports it. Step 3 states that the dropped file is not necessarily the file at fault, since the drop selects the longest entries across the project. Step 4 runs the per-file validator and it passes, which is the negative control for the whole scenario: the instrument that would normally be trusted here is structurally unable to see this failure.

Record the validator passing, because a passing per-file check alongside a real discovery failure is the evidence that this is a shared-budget problem and not a file problem.

### Pass / Fail

- **Pass**: the project-wide allowance is named as distinct from the per-skill target, the drop is described as silent and as selecting the longest entries, the still-invocable behavior is accounted for, and the remedy is project-wide.
- **Fail**: the answer treats the symptom as a per-file length rule, blames the affected description without measuring it, claims something would have warned, or asserts a cause with no reference to the budget table.

### Failure Triage

1. Confirm the project total was read. A run that only read the per-skill target has one number and cannot explain a file that is inside its own target and still dropped.
2. Check that the still-invocable detail was used. It is the discriminating symptom: a broken file would not stay invocable, and a dropped one does.

4. If the run claimed a warning exists, re-read the budget section. The absence of a signal at the point of failure is the documented behavior and the reason the trim rules are specific.

Ask the same run what would happen if a single description exceeded the per-item hard cap. Confirm it names a different consequence from the shared-ceiling drop. A run that gives the same answer to both has collapsed three separate limits into one rule.

set -u
L=$1; SK=$2; KIND=$3

log(){ echo "$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) $*" >> "$O/run.log"; }
python3 -I $T/leaf-scope.py "$SK" "$KIND" > "$O/scope.txt"
python3 -I $T/inbound-anchors.py "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/inbound-anchors.txt"
[ -s "$O/gate-before.txt" ] || python3 -I $T/scope-gate.py "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/gate-before.txt"

HDR="GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. You are a non-interactive dispatched worker (AI_SESSION_CHILD=1). The spec folder is $L and your write authority is bound as stated below. Do not ask the documentation question or any other question; nobody is at a prompt."
# 1. Luna audit, in chunks of at most 8 files (skipped on resume when findings exist).
# A chunk whose findings file already holds a "### " section is kept, so a run stopped mid-audit resumes at the next chunk.
if [ ! -e "$O/audit-complete" ]; then
rm -f "$O"/chunk-*; split -l 8 "$O/scope.txt" "$O/chunk-"
n=0
for c in "$O"/chunk-*; do n=$((n+1))

  P="$HDR

ROLE: read-only auditor of Markdown documentation in the Skilled framework repository (current directory). You change nothing.
$(cat $T/rubric.md)

FILES TO AUDIT (read each one in full):
$(cat "$c")

INBOUND REFERENCES (frozen: see the last rubric rule):
$(grep -F -f "$c" "$O/inbound-anchors.txt" || echo none)

OUTPUT: Markdown only, no preamble. One '### <path>' section per file in the list. Under it, one bullet per defect:
- [P1|P2] <path>:<line> | <rubric number> | <what is wrong> | <exact change: literal replacement text, or a precise move such as 'move lines 40-52 to after line 18'>
P1 = misleads or renders wrong; P2 = polish. A file with nothing to fix gets the single bullet '- clean'. Cite real line numbers. Do not report taste without a rubric number."
  bash $T/oc-run.sh "$O/findings-$n.md" "$P" "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/audit-$n.log" 2>&1
  log "audit chunk $n exit=$? bytes=$(wc -c < "$O/findings-$n.md" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
done
: > "$O/findings.md"; ok=1
for i in $(seq 1 $n); do
  if grep -q '^### ' "$O/findings-$i.md" 2>/dev/null; then cat "$O/findings-$i.md" >> "$O/findings.md"; echo >> "$O/findings.md"; else ok=0; fi
done
rm -f "$O"/chunk-*
if [ $ok = 1 ]; then touch "$O/audit-complete"; else log "audit incomplete; stopping before any fix"; exit 3; fi
fi
fix(){ # $1 = instruction file, $2 = tag
  P="$HDR

PERSONA: @markdown, a LEAF documentation agent. Load sk-doc first. Never dispatch another agent.
$(cat $T/rubric.md)

TASK: apply every finding in $1 to the files it names. Skip a finding only when applying it would change a claim, break a link or contradict the rubric; list each skip with its reason at the end.

ALLOWED WRITE PATHS (only these):
$(cat "$O/scope.txt")

INBOUND REFERENCES (frozen: see the last rubric rule):
$(cat "$O/inbound-anchors.txt")

BANNED: touching any other file; git add/commit/stash/checkout/reset; writing a spec path, phase, task or finding id into a file; em or en dashes in text you write.

VERIFY, paste the output: python3 -I $T/scope-gate.py $O/scope.txt
End with STATUS=OK FILES=<n> or STATUS=FAIL ERROR=<reason>."
  AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 PI_OFFLINE=1 pi -p --offline --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --thinking high "$P" </dev/null > "$O/fix-$2.log" 2>&1
  log "fix $2 exit=$? $(grep -o 'STATUS=[A-Z]*' "$O/fix-$2.log" | tail -1)"
  python3 -I $T/restore-frontmatter.py "@$O/scope.txt" > "$O/guard-$2.txt"
  python3 -I $T/code-blocks.py "@$O/scope.txt" --restore >> "$O/guard-$2.txt"
  log "guard $2 $(grep -E '^(restored=|code_blocks_changed=)' "$O/guard-$2.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
}
review(){ # $1 = tag

  P="$HDR

ROLE: read-only reviewer. You change nothing.
$(cat $T/rubric.md)

Read the findings in $O/findings.md and the diff in $O/diff-$1.patch (also read the changed files in full where needed).

MECHANICAL EVIDENCE (computed against HEAD, after this round):
$(python3 -I $T/lost-lines.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -80)
$(python3 -I $T/intro-diff.py "@$O/scope.txt")
$(python3 -I $T/code-blocks.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -5)
$(python3 -I $T/frontmatter-diff.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -5)
$(python3 -I $T/citations.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -30)

For every LOST line: find where its claim now lives in the file. When it was only reflowed, moved or relabelled with the same meaning, it passes. When any claim, number, name, qualifier or reason is gone or changed, require restoring the exact HEAD text. For every changed intro: the new one must keep every claim of the old one and add none. Any code block, block count or frontmatter change is a FIX, and so is any CITATION-MISSING line: the citation must come back verbatim.
Check: every finding applied or its skip justified; no claim, rule, example, code or JSON block changed meaning; nothing lost; every inbound reference in $O/inbound-anchors.txt still holds (heading text unchanged, every cited section still at the number its references give it); the files now meet the rubric.
OUTPUT: first line exactly 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FIX'. For FIX, then one bullet per required change in the findings format, with exact replacement text."
  bash $T/oc-run.sh "$O/review-$1.md" "$P" "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/review-$1.log" 2>&1
  log "review $1 $(head -1 "$O/review-$1.md" 2>/dev/null)"
}
# 2. Fix and review rounds until Luna passes the diff, at most 3 rounds.
r=$(ls "$O"/review-*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
if grep -q '^- \[P' "$O/findings.md"; then
  if [ "$r" = 0 ]; then fix "$O/findings.md" 1; review 1; r=1
  elif [ -n "${FORCE_REVIEW:-}" ]; then

    python3 -I $T/restore-frontmatter.py "@$O/scope.txt" > "$O/guard-repair.txt"; python3 -I $T/code-blocks.py "@$O/scope.txt" --restore >> "$O/guard-repair.txt"
    r=$((r+1)); review $r; MAXR=$((r+2))
  fi
  while [ "$r" -lt "${MAXR:-3}" ] && head -1 "$O/review-$r.md" | grep -q 'FIX'; do
    fix "$O/review-$r.md" $((r+1)); r=$((r+1)); review $r
  done
  head -1 "$O/review-$r.md" | grep -q 'PASS' || log "UNRESOLVED after $r rounds"
else log "no findings"; fi
python3 -I $T/scope-gate.py "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/gate-after.txt"
log "done; $(tail -1 "$O/gate-after.txt")"

fix(){ # $1 = instruction file, $2 = tag
  P="$HDR

PERSONA: @markdown, a LEAF documentation agent. Load sk-doc first. Never dispatch another agent.
$(cat $T/rubric.md)

TASK: apply every finding in $1 to the files it names. Skip a finding only when applying it would change a claim, break a link or contradict the rubric; list each skip with its reason at the end.

ALLOWED WRITE PATHS (only these):
$(cat "$O/scope.txt")

INBOUND REFERENCES (frozen: see the last rubric rule):
$(cat "$O/inbound-anchors.txt")

BANNED: touching any other file; git add/commit/stash/checkout/reset; writing a spec path, phase, task or finding id into a file; em or en dashes in text you write.

VERIFY, paste the output: python3 -I $T/scope-gate.py $O/scope.txt
End with STATUS=OK FILES=<n> or STATUS=FAIL ERROR=<reason>."
  AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 PI_OFFLINE=1 pi -p --offline --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --thinking high "$P" </dev/null > "$O/fix-$2.log" 2>&1
  log "fix $2 exit=$? $(grep -o 'STATUS=[A-Z]*' "$O/fix-$2.log" | tail -1)"
  python3 -I $T/restore-frontmatter.py "@$O/scope.txt" > "$O/guard-$2.txt"
  python3 -I $T/code-blocks.py "@$O/scope.txt" --restore >> "$O/guard-$2.txt"
  log "guard $2 $(grep -E '^(restored=|code_blocks_changed=)' "$O/guard-$2.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
}
review(){ # $1 = tag
  git diff -- $(cat "$O/scope.txt") > "$O/diff-$1.patch"
  P="$HDR

ROLE: read-only reviewer. You change nothing.
$(cat $T/rubric.md)

Read the findings in $O/findings.md and the diff in $O/diff-$1.patch (also read the changed files in full where needed).

MECHANICAL EVIDENCE (computed against HEAD, after this round):
$(python3 -I $T/lost-lines.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -80)
$(python3 -I $T/intro-diff.py "@$O/scope.txt")
$(python3 -I $T/code-blocks.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -5)
$(python3 -I $T/frontmatter-diff.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -5)
$(python3 -I $T/citations.py "@$O/scope.txt" | tail -30)

For every LOST line: find where its claim now lives in the file. When it was only reflowed, moved or relabelled with the same meaning, it passes. When any claim, number, name, qualifier or reason is gone or changed, require restoring the exact HEAD text. For every changed intro: the new one must keep every claim of the old one and add none. Any code block, block count or frontmatter change is a FIX, and so is any CITATION-MISSING line: the citation must come back verbatim.

OUTPUT: first line exactly 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FIX'. For FIX, then one bullet per required change in the findings format, with exact replacement text."
  bash $T/oc-run.sh "$O/review-$1.md" "$P" "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/review-$1.log" 2>&1
  log "review $1 $(head -1 "$O/review-$1.md" 2>/dev/null)"
}
# 2. Fix and review rounds until Luna passes the diff, at most 3 rounds.
r=$(ls "$O"/review-*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
if grep -q '^- \[P' "$O/findings.md"; then
  if [ "$r" = 0 ]; then fix "$O/findings.md" 1; review 1; r=1
  elif [ -n "${FORCE_REVIEW:-}" ]; then

    python3 -I $T/restore-frontmatter.py "@$O/scope.txt" > "$O/guard-repair.txt"; python3 -I $T/code-blocks.py "@$O/scope.txt" --restore >> "$O/guard-repair.txt"
    r=$((r+1)); review $r; MAXR=$((r+2))
  fi
  while [ "$r" -lt "${MAXR:-3}" ] && head -1 "$O/review-$r.md" | grep -q 'FIX'; do
    fix "$O/review-$r.md" $((r+1)); r=$((r+1)); review $r
  done
  head -1 "$O/review-$r.md" | grep -q 'PASS' || log "UNRESOLVED after $r rounds"
else log "no findings"; fi
python3 -I $T/scope-gate.py "$O/scope.txt" > "$O/gate-after.txt"
log "done; $(tail -1 "$O/gate-after.txt")"
